newsitem.title: USA: Pharmacia & Upjohn adopts rights plan.
newsitem.headline: Pharmacia & Upjohn adopts rights plan.

text.p: Pharmacia & Upjohn Inc said Tuesday its board of directors had adopted a shareholder protection rights plan.
The rights plan was not adopted in response to any specific effort to acquire control of the pharmaceutical company, Pharmacia & Upjohn said in a statement received here.
The plan is intended to preserve investment values and protect stockholders in the event an attempt is made to acquire the company without offering fair value to all stockholders, the company said.
The plan encourages possible acquirers to negotiate with directors in advance of an unsolicited acquisition attempt.

The plan calls for each holder of record of Pharmacia & Upjohn common stock (including Swedish Depository Shares representing shares of common stock) on March 7, 1997, to receive a divdend distribution of one right for each share held in the company. The rights will not be immediately exercisable but should any person or group acquire 15 percent or more of the company's outstanding stock, each right can be exercised to purchase company stock at 50 percent discount.

Under such a scenario, the acquiring person or group would not be entitled to the same treatment, and would face the threat of significant dilution of both its financial investment and voting power. This creates a strong incentive for any person or group to negotiate with the company prior to crossing the 15 percent ownership threshold, the company said.

Pharmacia & Upjohn said the rights plan does not weaken the company's financial strength or interfere with its business plans. The issuance of these rights has no dilutive effect, will not affect reported earnings per share or change the way in which Pharmacia & Upjohn shares are traded.
The company also said its directors approved payment of a regular quarterly dividend of $0.27 per share on May 2, 1997 to stockholders of record on April 8, 1997.

The board also said it elected two new officers, Toni Weitzberg, senior vice president and president of Pharma product center Sweden, and Jorgen Johnsson, senior vice president and president of consumer healthcare.

Pharmacia & Upjohn provides human health care and related products, and operates worldwide. The company has a corporate management center in London, and research and manufacturing centers in the United States, Sweden and Italy.
